transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-28
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Maria Lopez (Horizon Head of AI), Ethan Shaw (CTO), Priya Nair (Clinical Data Lead)

Summary: quick discovery / POC scoping focused on quality evaluation plan. Discussed success criteria, workload sizing, golden prompts, hallucination/format checks, scoring approach, timelines and security/network constraints. Action items and next steps at end.

00:00 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about 50 minutes, we wanted to walk through what a POC could look like, focus today on quality eval plan — golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination/format checks, scoring — and align on success criteria and timing.
00:14 Dr. Maria: thanks Alex, excited. we have been piloting a few assistants internally but main ask is clinical note summarization and coding suggestions; accuracy and no hallucinations are musts.
00:30 Ethan: yeah from infra side we also need to understand VPC/on-prem constraints and what data leaves our network.
00:38 Alex: totally — we support private deployments, dedicated, or hosted with strong controls, we'll get into that. Samir is on to cover the benchmarks and eval harness.
00:46 Samir: hi all, quick caveat — transcription may have some noise, i might say kv cache when i mean k/v cache, so just flag me if anything is off. ok, starting with success criteria — based on your notes earlier we think top-line should be: 1) ROUGE-L F1 > 0.78 on clinical summarization for the golden set, 2) hallucination rate under 1% measured by entity hallucination checks, 3) structured output format compliance > 98% for coded outputs. is that aligned?
01:12 Dr. Maria: sounds reasonable, though denote we weight hallucinations more heavily — we prefer stricter threshold there even if ROUGE a little lower.
01:22 Priya: also want metrics for safety: PHI leakage checks, redaction pass/fail, and auditability of predictions with trace to source sentence.
01:30 Samir: good calls. for workload sizing — can you confirm expected qps and average doc length? on your intake you mentioned 200 daily users and batch nightly jobs of ~10k notes?
01:44 Priya: current: approx 150 clinicians daily, peak ~300, synchronous summarization calls maybe 2-3 qps, but we also have bulk nightly processing for coding — about 8k-12k notes daily. median note length ~700 tokens, 95p < 2,500 tokens.
02:03 Alex: that helps. for the POC we recommend two parallel tracks: a 2-week quality eval using your golden prompt set and 500-1,000 representative notes, and a 4-week throughput benchmark on dedicated capacity if you want SLA-like numbers. start with quality.
02:22 Ethan: what's included in the quality eval harness?
02:26 Samir: we usually run: 1) golden prompt checks — defined set of prompts and expected reference outputs, 2) regression tests where we compare current model variants to baseline (your existing model or current in-prod), 3) hallucination detection — automated entity overlap and entailment checks plus human adjudication on a random sample, 4) format/schema validation for structured outputs, 5) scoring approach combining automatic metrics and human score for critical failures.
02:55 Dr. Maria: can you give more detail on hallucination checks? that's the big worry.
03:00 Samir: sure — automated pipeline: extract named entities and procedures from source note and model output, compute overlap and novel-entity rate; run an entailment model to see if claims in summary are supported by sources; mark as potential hallucination if novel-entity-rate > threshold or entailment score < threshold. then we sample flagged and unflagged for human review to estimate false positives/negatives. we typically aim for measured hallucination < 1% at 95% CI.
03:30 Priya: okay, for human adjudication who do you use? internal SMEs?
03:34 Samir: we can do a blended approach — you can provide internal SMEs for clinical adjudication and we can use contractor clinical annotators for volume. annotations are logged with provenance in the eval harness.
03:45 Ethan: about security — we need to know if model weights or data leave our VPC when using hosted Redwood.
03:51 Alex: hosted means data leaves VPC encrypted, stored in Redwood tenancy, with SOC2 and controls — but for stricter requirements we can do Redwood Private with customer-managed VPC or on-prem. for the POC, many customers do a private connection (VPC peering / PrivateLink) so data flows over dedicated network and logs are retained per your policy. we'll share the security whitepaper.
04:12 Dr. Maria: good. on scoring approach, you mentioned combining auto metrics and human score. how do you weight them?
04:19 Samir: common approach: automatic metrics (ROUGE / BERTScore / exact entity match) for broad coverage — these are weighted at ~40% of the total score. human quality (factuality, clinical harm risk, readability, format compliance) gets ~60%. but we can tune those weights — for you i'd recommend 70% human on factuality + hallucination risk, 20% automated, 10% format checks, because hallucinations are critical.
04:49 Priya: yes that weighting seems right. also we need per-case severity: if hallucination mentions a wrong med vs minor date mismatch — severity levels matter.
04:58 Samir: we'll include severity buckets in the adjudication rubric: minor/medium/critical with examples. that will feed into an SLA pass/fail and an aggregate risk score.
05:10 Alex: timeline idea: week 0 - kickoff and data transfer + access, week 1-2 - run golden prompt eval on 500 samples + human adjudication, week 3 - model iteration and regression test with improved prompts/quantization profile, week 4 - report and decision. if you want throughput benchmarking on dedicated nodes add another 2 weeks. does that fit your org timeline?
05:28 Dr. Maria: yes, we want to review results before end of january, so this aligns.
05:35 Ethan: about environment — we'll likely want to run the quality eval in your hosted sandbox initially, then switch to private if needed. network team needs to confirm firewall rules.
05:45 Alex: noted, action for Ethan to confirm network. also we will provide a benchmark harness repo with ingestion scripts; Samir will lead bench setup.
05:55 Priya: what metrics will you show in the POC report?
06:00 Samir: we'll provide: aggregate ROUGE/BERTScore distributions, hallucination rate + sample-level flags, format compliance %, latency P50/P95 for sample lengths, cost per note estimate, and an error-trace table tying outputs back to source sentences. plus human adjudication detail and severity breakdown.
06:18 Dr. Maria: do you support scoring on structured outputs? we need CCI codes and ICD-10 match rates.
06:23 Samir: yes — structured outputs can be validated against taxonomy and we compute exact-match and normalized match (for synonyms). we'll provide a mapping layer if your codes deviate from common standards.
06:34 Ethan: curious about model variants — are you suggesting we run multiple models concurrently?
06:38 Samir: for the POC we often run 2 variants: 1) a larger model with higher factuality (nucleus 0.95) as candidate and 2) a faster quantized model for latency/cost tradeoffs. both get the same eval harness; regression compares them to your baseline.
06:52 Dr. Maria: one more on prompts: can you show example golden prompts?
06:56 Samir: yes, i'll share a shell of golden prompts: e.g., "Summarize the clinical note in 3 bullets focusing on history, assessment, plan. Mention only items present in note. If data not present say 'not documented'." then include explicit schema for coding output: JSON with fields diagnosis_codes:[], plan_items:[], severity_score:int. we will include negative examples and adversarial prompts to test hallucination.
07:23 Priya: negative examples are helpful — can you run stress tests like partial notes, redacted data, and concatenated notes to see failure modes?
07:29 Samir: absolutely, stress tests are part of the harness — partial inputs, template injection, long-context truncation. we'll log failure modes and recommendations (prompt edits, chunking strategies, caching).
07:40 Ethan: regarding cost estimates — do you provide cost per-token or per-note model?
07:45 Alex: yes, the POC report includes cost per note based on observed token consumption and model choice, and estimated monthly cost at scale. we'll give three profiles: hosted on curated model, dedicated reserved capacity, and private on-prem equivalent.
07:58 Dr. Maria: about auditing — we need immutable audit logs for every inference and a way to re-run inference for a given note with the same model / seed. do you keep seeds / deterministic runs?
08:09 Samir: we keep request-level logs and can snapshot model versions and prompt sets used; for deterministic reproductions we recommend fixed seeding and capturing runtime config; for sampling-based modes exact determinism may not be possible but we can provide a stable variant.
08:24 Priya: one constraint — we cannot share PHI to third-party annotators, so any human adjudication for flagged hallucinations must be done by our internal SME or by annotators under a BAA.
08:32 Alex: understood — we'll note BAA options and also can use your internal SMEs for sensitive sample review.
08:37 Dr. Maria: ok, what does the golden prompt set look like? how many prompts do you suggest?
08:41 Samir: for POC we suggest ~10-20 golden prompts covering core tasks and edge cases. prompts include positive controls (straightforward summarization), negative controls (prompt-injection attempts), format-only prompts to test JSON schema, and adversarial prompts. we'll provide a template and you can add clinic-specific variants.
09:00 Priya: scoring rubrics please — how will humans score hallucination severity?
09:05 Samir: we'll give a 1-5 severity scale with buckets and examples: 1 = cosmetic, 3 = incorrect med/dose (non-critical), 5 = suggest harmful action; each sample gets severity tag and binary factuality pass/fail. aggregated metrics: % critical hallucinations, weighted hallucination score, and overall pass threshold.
09:22 Dr. Maria: what about regression tests? when you say regression, do you mean comparing to our current model?
09:25 Samir: yes either your current in-prod model or a baseline we select. regression tests are automatic metrics + human sample comparison; if model A improves on factuality but worsens format compliance we call it out.
09:36 Alex: quick note on format checks — we use JSON schema validators, and also semantic validators that check field types and controlled vocabs. failures are logged with sample and line.
09:46 Ethan: network question — for private deployment do you need any special ports open?
09:49 Alex: typically we ask for HTTPS outbound to Redwood control plane and specific ports for gRPC or private link; Samir will post the exact firewall matrix.
10:00 Priya: about the sample set — we will need guidance on anonymization, and how to slice samples to ensure coverage of different note types.
10:07 Samir: we'll provide a sample selection guide: stratify by specialty, note length, inpatient vs outpatient, and include edge cases like template-heavy notes. recommend 500 core golden samples + 500 randomized for regression.
10:20 Dr. Maria: can you show an example of the POC report layout?
10:23 Alex: we'll share a template: Executive summary, Key metrics (automated + human), Hallucination findings, Severity breakdown, Latency & cost, Recommendations & next steps.
10:33 Priya: for the adjudication UI, do you have a tool?
10:36 Samir: yes we have a lightweight adjudication dashboard where SMEs see source note, model output side-by-side, tag factuality, severity, and free-text notes. it's exportable as csv.
10:46 Ethan: can you commit to data retention policies for the POC? we need retention under 90 days unless we agree otherwise.
10:52 Alex: yes for POC we typically set 30-90 day retention and can adjust. we'll put this in SOW.
10:58 Dr. Maria: ok let's try to lock down immediate deliverables.
11:01 Alex: agreed — action list recap: Alex send SOW/pricing, Samir send harness + golden prompt template, Horizon to supply 500 samples anonymized, Ethan confirm networking, schedule kickoff week of 2027-01-11.
11:15 Priya: one last question — will you instrument hallucination detectors during inference or post-hoc?
11:19 Samir: both — we run post-hoc automated checks as part of the eval harness, and we can optionally instrument lightweight checks in-path for near-real-time flagging. for the POC we'll start post-hoc.
11:30 Dr. Maria: great, thanks, this was useful.
11:34 Alex: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and scheduling.

End of transcript.
